title: Fail the build when an every-turn rule is reachable only from a reference
action: Per T5 write a NEW suite scripts/tests/test_always_loaded_rules.mjs that FAILS -- exit non-zero -- when a rule that applies every turn is reachable only from a reference file and not from the always-loaded operating block. run_verify.mjs auto-discovers suites by globbing test_*.mjs under scripts/tests/, so do not edit it. This targets the root cause the whole feature came from: the progress-tick contract was specified as mandatory per-step, lived only in a reference, and the one check that would have caught it (skill_lint) both mismatched and always exits 0 -- so the gap survived indefinitely with the warning firing the entire time. Derive the rule set rather than hardcoding it: a hardcoded list of the very thing being checked for drift is the defect this suite exists to catch, one level up. The Deferred-To-Planning question is yours to settle and to record: an explicit every-turn marker in the doctrine source is checkable but must itself be maintained; deriving from the rule's own wording is self-updating but fragile. Pick one, implement it, and say in your report which you chose and why. Per T6 the suite must NOT claim to enforce tick emission -- nothing in the repo observes agent chat output, so it proves reachability only. If you write a header comment, say that limit plainly there. The suite must be GREEN against the repo as it stands after tci-1 and tci-2 land, and must FAIL when a rule is moved back behind a reference -- prove both directions by temporarily reverting one and restoring it.

truths: node scripts/tests/test_always_loaded_rules.mjs exits 0 against the repo as it stands
It exits non-zero when an every-turn rule is moved out of the block, naming that rule
The suite runs in the full verify chain via glob discovery
Nothing in the suite claims to verify that a tick was emitted

prohibitions: No hardcoded list of rules that would need editing whenever doctrine changes

trace.outcome: New blocking suite fails the build when a rule the doctrine's own wording says applies every turn is reachable only from an on-demand reference. Rule set derived (corpus walked, sections found by wording, pointers read off the block); the single seed is a per-turn scope vocabulary, no rule roster. Header states the T6 limit: proves reachability, never emission. Green on the tree; red naming the Progress ticks section against both the real pre-tci-1 block and a surgical strip of rule 17.
deviations: Also regenerated scripts/impact-registry.json (node scripts/impact_registry.mjs --write). Adding any file discovered as a suite makes the committed registry stale, which turns scripts/tests/test_impact_registry.mjs red and fails the CI step 'Check impact registry freshness' (.github/workflows/ci.yml:57). Deviation rule 3 (blocking issue in the path) - auto-fixed. Diff is purely additive: 8 insertions, one new key, 202 -> 203 files.

Settled the cell's Deferred-To-Planning question as DERIVATION FROM WORDING rather than an authored every-turn marker, and recorded the reasoning in the suite header: a marker's failure mode is silence, which is the same defect this suite exists to catch one level up; wording derivation fails toward a red build instead.

Declared seed, per the cell's fallback clause: EVERY_TURN_PHRASES (6 regexes for how English states per-turn scope). A domain fact about wording, not a location and not a roster - no rule name, heading, file path, or rule count is hardcoded. Bare 'every step' / 'per step' were tested and rejected from the seed: they produced 4 false positives (a numbered-step cross-reference, a one-shot procedural list, a bypass-immunity clause, a promotion-advice line).

Provenance ledgers are skipped via self-declaration (isProvenanceLedger matches the file's own 'maps each body rule to the decision' intro), never by filename - a ledger that drops the declaration gets scanned. The exclusion fails toward flagging, never toward silence.

skills/*/SKILL.md bodies are deliberately out of scope (different tier, different pointer convention: they cite AGENTS.md rule numbers rather than being pointed at). Stated as a scope limit in the header so the suite does not read as broader than it is.
trace.friction: The configured generation-tier model 'opus-4-5' is not an accepted value for the Agent tool's model param (only sonnet/opus/haiku/fable), so bee-model-guard refuses any generation-tier dispatch from this runtime; had to re-route the investigation to the review tier.
